briefings.tldr: While global inflation is driven by geopolitical triggers like Middle East tensions and energy volatility, its impacts vary widely between high-demand economies like the US and low-inflation states like China, requiring a mix of targeted fiscal policies, renewable energy investments, and innovative institutional frameworks to protect vulnerable populations.

briefings.title: The Next Billion Jobs

people.name: Faisal Alibrahim
people.role: Minister of Economy and Planning of Saudi Arabia

briefings.tldr: While the World Bank projects a 400 million youth job shortfall globally, the rapid expansion of AI and digital platforms offers an unprecedented engine for productivity and employment, provided governments, businesses, and educational institutions aggressively coordinate to prioritize entrepreneurship, continuous reskilling, and human-centric industrial policies.

briefings.title: What Next for the Middle East?

people.name: Faisal Alibrahim
people.role: Minister of Economy and Planning of Saudi Arabia

people.name: Sigrid Kaag
people.role: Senior Humanitarian and Reconstruction Coordinator for Gaza, United Nations

briefings.tldr: Following a highly disruptive regional war in early 2026, the Middle East is navigating a fragile diplomatic off-ramp while rapidly accelerating domestic infrastructure, logistics, and renewable energy projects to build long-term economic resilience.
